name: Dana Okafor
companyContext: Mid-size manufacturer of packaging, 3 plants and a central distribution centre, about 900 hourly staff. The COO, Helen Price, is drowning in vendor requests.
budget: Not her budget. She knows the COO is reviewing labour costs this quarter because she builds the board pack.
targets: Protect Helen's calendar. Her rule: no vendor meeting unless it is clearly relevant to a current priority.
competingVendors: Three other workforce vendors have called this month
personality: Polite, quick, firm. Has a script for vendors. Will help someone who is clear, specific and respectful of her time; blocks anyone vague or pushy.
situation: The rep is calling the COO's office line; Dana answers. She is between two meetings.
secretlyWants: To bring Helen something genuinely useful for the labour-cost review so she looks good, without wasting Helen's time.
withholds: That labour costs are on the board agenda next month (only shares if the rep asks a smart question about current priorities).
That Helen prefers a one-page summary before any meeting (only shares if the rep asks how Helen likes to receive information).
That the distribution centre manager, Raj, is the person who actually feels the scheduling pain (only shares if the rep asks who else is involved).
hangsUpWhen: The rep tries to trick her (pretends to know Helen, claims a meeting was already agreed, or lies about the reason for calling)
The rep is condescending to her as 'just the assistant'
The rep talks for more than 30 seconds straight without letting her speak
earnsNextStep: The rep is honest that this is a sales call
The rep explains in one sentence why it matters to Helen now
The rep treats Dana as a decision-shaper and asks for her advice
speechStyle: Fast, efficient, polite. Often says she has two minutes. Ends the call if it drifts.
